headline: No clear direction, and a jumpy market
text: US futures are up ahead of the open (S&P +0.40%, Nasdaq +0.66%), with Europe higher and Asia mostly up.
Helping: S&P 500 vs 200-day, Stocks above 200-day. Weighing: Copper, VIX, VIX curve.

Expect a jumpy session: the VIX is high at 25.5, SPY options gamma is negative (dealers' hedging makes moves bigger), the VIX curve is inverted. Gaps and reversals are common in these conditions, so a small early move says little.
Reporting: before the open TJX, LOW, TGT; after the close PANW, P.
Options price a typical day of about ±1.7% for the S&P 500 (about 7,246–7,494); historically about 82% of days stay inside that.
On past days with VIX between 25 and 30 (since 1990, 867 days), the next session closed higher 52% of the time (all days: 54%), with a typical move of 0.9% (all days: 0.5%).

drivers.name: US futures
drivers.note: S&P +0.40% · Nasdaq +0.66% vs the last close. The clearest hint of how the day opens.

drivers.name: Dollar index
drivers.note: A sharply stronger dollar usually weighs on US stocks (tighter money, weaker overseas earnings).

drivers.name: 10-year yield
drivers.note: At 5.10%. Fast-rising yields hurt growth and tech stocks; falling yields help them.

drivers.name: WTI oil
drivers.note: $84.33. A big oil jump feeds inflation worries; energy stocks move with it.

drivers.name: Gold
drivers.note: $3762. A strong gold bid often means investors are looking for safety.

drivers.name: Copper
drivers.note: “Dr. Copper”: rising copper = traders expect more growth.

drivers.name: Bitcoin
drivers.note: Trades all weekend and night: a read on risk appetite while Wall Street is shut.

drivers.name: S&P 500 vs 200-day
drivers.note: Above the 200-day = long-term uptrend: dips have tended to get bought.

drivers.name: Stocks above 200-day
drivers.note: How many big US stocks are in their own uptrend.

drivers.name: VIX
drivers.note: Below 16 calm, above 25 nervous, above 30 fear.

drivers.name: VIX curve
drivers.note: Inverted (above 1): traders pay more for protection this month than for later months. Usually only in sell-offs.

drivers.name: Market mood
drivers.note: Fear: the site's 0–100 fear/greed gauge from 10 readings. Extremes often mark turning points, so it sets the tone rather than the direction.

levels.name: SPY call wall
levels.note: Biggest call position: often acts as a ceiling.

levels.name: SPY gamma flip
levels.note: Above it dealers calm moves down; below it they speed them up.

levels.name: SPY put wall
levels.note: Biggest put position: often acts as a floor; a break can speed up selling.

levels.name: SPY call wall by today's volume
levels.note: Where today's new call trading is concentrated: shows the ceiling shifting during the session.

scenarios.text: If SPY breaks below 730 (put wall), selling can speed up.
If SPY gets back above 756 (gamma flip), moves tend to calm and dips get bought.
Yesterday's S&P 500 range was 7,288–7,415: a break of either end is the first real sign of direction.

tips: Size smaller than usual and use the “wrong if” level on every alert.
Crypto: fear & greed 11 (Extreme Fear), Bitcoin −0.3% in 24h, funding 0.004%.
